b.13e6e2f4d6:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>V</c>írginis Proles, Opiféxque Matris,
Virgo quem gessit, peperítque Virgo:
Vírginis festum cánimus trophǽum
Accipe votum.

<h>H</h>æc tua Virgo dúplici beáta
Sorte, dum gestit frágilem domáre
Córporis sexum, dómuit cruéntum
Corpóre sæclum.

<h>U</h>nde nec mortem, nec amíca mortis
Sæva pœnárum génera pavéscens,
Sánguine fuso méruit sacrátum
Scándere cælum.

<h>H</h>uius obténtu, Deus alme, nostris
Parce iam culpis, vítia remíttens,
Quo tibi puri resonémus almum
Péctoris hymnum.

<h>G</h>lória Patri genitǽque Proli,
Et tibi compar utriúsque semper
Spíritus alme, Deus unus, omni
Témpore sæcli.
Amen.
b.1d2384938a:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>S</c>on of a virgin, maker of thy mother,
Thou, rod and blossom from a stem unstainèd,
While we a Virgin's triumphs are rehearsing,
Hear our petition!

<h>L</h>o, on thy handmaid fell a two-fold blessing,
Who, in her body vanquishing the weakness,
In that same body, grace from heaven obtaining,
Bore the world witness.

<h>D</h>eath, nor the rending pains of death appalled her;
Bondage and torment found her undefeated:
So by the shedding of her blood attained she
Heavenly guerdon.

<h>F</h>ountain of mercy, hear the prayers she offers;
Purge our offences, pardon our transgressions,
So that hereafter we to thee may render
Praise with thanksgiving.

<h>T</h>hou, the All-Father, thou, the One-Begotten,
Thou, Holy Spirit, Three in One co-equal,
Glory be henceforth thine through all the ages,
World without ending.
Amen.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro Ecclesiástici
<r>Sir 51:1-7</r>
<n>1</n> Confitébor tibi, Dómine, Rex, et collaudábo te Deum Salvatórem meum.
<n>2</n> Confitébor nómini tuo: quóniam adiútor et protéctor factus es mihi,
<n>3</n> Et liberásti corpus meum a perditióne, a láqueo linguæ iníquæ et a lábiis operántium mendácium, et in conspéctu astántium factus es mihi adiútor.
<n>4</n> Et liberásti me secúndum multitúdinem misericórdiæ nóminis tui a rugiéntibus, præparátis ad escam:
<n>5</n> De mánibus quæréntium ánimam meam, et de portis tribulatiónum, quæ circumdedérunt me;
<n>6</n> A pressúra flammæ, quæ circúmdedit me, et in médio ignis non sum æstuáta;
<n>7</n> De altitúdine ventris ínferi, et a lingua coinquináta, et a verbo mendácii, a rege iníquo, et a lingua iniústa.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Cantántibus órganis, Cæcília virgo in corde suo soli Dómino decantábat, dicens:
* Fiat, Dómine, cor meum et corpus meum immaculátum, ut non confúndar.
<r>℣.</r> Biduánis et triduánis ieiúniis orans, commendábat Dómino quod timébat.
<r>℟.</r> Fiat, Dómine, cor meum et corpus meum immaculátum, ut non confúndar.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the book of Ecclesiasticus
<r>Sir 51:1-7</r>
<n>1</n> A prayer of Jesus the son of Sirach. I will give glory to thee, O Lord, O King, and I will praise thee, O God my Saviour.
<n>2</n> I will give glory to thy name: for thou hast been a helper and protector to me.
<n>3</n> And hast preserved my body from destruction, from the snare of an unjust tongue, and from the lips of them that forge lies, and in the sight of them that stood by, thou hast been my helper.
<n>4</n> And thou hast delivered me, according to the multitude of the mercy of thy name, from them that did roar, prepared to devour.
<n>5</n> Out of the hands of them that sought my life, and from the gates of afflictions, which compassed me about:
<n>6</n> From the oppression of the flame which surrounded me, and in the midst of the fire I was not burnt.
<n>7</n> From the depth of the belly of hell, and from an unclean tongue, and from lying words, from an unjust king, and from a slanderous tongue:
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> The musicians played, and the maiden Cecilia sang in her heart unto the Lord alone, saying:
* Lord, let my heart and my body be undefiled, that I be not ashamed.
<r>℣.</r> She fasted and prayed for two days and three days together, committing the cause of her fear unto the Lord.
<r>℟.</r> Lord, let my heart and my body be undefiled, that I be not ashamed.

<r>Sir 51:8-12</r>
<n>8</n> Laudábit usque ad mortem ánima mea Dóminum,
<n>9</n> Et vita mea appropínquans erat in inférno deórsum.
<n>10</n> Circumdedérunt me úndique, et non erat qui adiuváret. Respíciens eram ad adiutórium hóminum, et non erat.
<n>11</n> Memoráta sum misericórdiæ tuæ, Dómine, et operatiónis tuæ, quæ a sǽculo sunt:
<n>12</n> Quóniam éruis sustinéntes te, Dómine, et líberas eos de mánibus géntium.
<r>Sir 51:13-17</r>
<n>13</n> Exaltásti super terram habitatiónem meam, et pro morte defluénte deprecáta sum.
<n>14</n> Invocávi Dóminum, Patrem Dómini mei, ut non derelínquat me in die tribulatiónis meæ, et in témpore superbórum, sine adiutório.
<n>15</n> Laudábo nomen tuum assídue, et collaudábo illud in confessióne, et exaudíta est orátio mea.
<n>16</n> Et liberásti me de perditióne, et eripuísti me de témpore iníquo.
<n>17</n> Proptérea confitébor, et laudem dicam tibi, et benedícam nómini Dómini.

<r>Sir 51:8-12</r>

<n>9</n> And my life was drawing near to hell beneath.
<n>10</n> They compassed me on every side, and there was no one that would help me. I looked for the succour of men, and there was none.
<n>11</n> I remembered thy mercy, O Lord, and thy works, which are from the beginning of the world.
<n>12</n> How thou deliverest them that wait for thee, O Lord, and savest them out of the hands of the nations.

<n>13</n> Thou hast exalted my dwelling place upon the earth and I have prayed for death to pass away.
<n>14</n> I called upon the Lord, the father of my Lord, that he would not leave me in the day of my trouble, and in the time of the proud without help.

<h>Reading 3</h>
<c>C</c>ecilia, a Roman virgin of noble birth, vowed her virginity to God at a very early age. Given in marriage against her will to Valerian, she persuaded him to leave her untouched and go to blessed Urban, the Pope, that when he had been baptized he might be worthy to see Cecilia's angelic protector. When Valerian had obtained this favor, he converted his brother Tiburtius to Christ, and a little later both were martyred under the prefect Almachius. But Cecilia was seized by the same prefect because she had distributed the two brothers' wealth to the poor, and orders were given to have her suffocated in a bath. When the heat dared not harm her, she was struck three times with an axe, and left half dead. After three days she received the palm of virginity and of martyrdom, and was buried in the cemetery of Callistus. Her body and those of Popes Urban and Lucius, and of Tiburtius, Valerian and Maximus were transferred by Pope Paschal I to the church in the City dedicated to St. Cecilia.
